MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  November 5, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday, October
15, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez and Mayor Gazeley. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. PRESENTATIONS

Presentation by Congresswoman Maxine Waters relative to federal legislation.

Congresswoman Maxine Waters stated that she is campaigning throughout the area. Lomita
and some other South Bay cities were added to her congressional district. Congresswoman
Waters added that Lomita Railroad Museum is a wonderful landmark that could be used as a
tourist attraction and potentially could be extended with the community center.

Congresswoman Waters asked City Council to consider supporting petition dealing with
sequestration. Ms. Waters added that it is important to support local communities and possible
budget cuts could affect federal funding provided to Lomita. Sequestration petition would allow
members of Congress to understand of how budget cuts could bring negative impact on local
communities.

Presentation by Walter Rosenkranz regarding Car2go car sharing program.

Walter Rosenkranz, car2consultant for car2go, provided overview of the car2go car sharing
program, the first fully automated, one-way, open-end, on-the-spot car sharing system, which
allows rental of the car on a short term basis. Mr. Rosenkranz added that this system allows on
demand mobility, “pay-as-you-drive” by a minute, with discounted rates for hourly and daily use.

  Page 1 of 8
 This system is all inclusive including vehicle rental, fuel, insurance, parking and maintenance.
Mr. Rosenkranz emphasized that car2go provides a flexible mobility solution while removing
vehicles for City streets.

Discussion followed regarding potential benefits of having car sharing program in the City of
Lomita, location for parking car2go cars and maintenance and repair of the vehicles.

Mayor Gazeley made a motion to bring this car sharing program for the next City Council
meeting. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Proclamation declaring the week of November 12, 2012 through November 18, 2012 as
Entrepreneurship Week in the City of Lomita.

Mayor Gazeley proclaimed the week of November 12, 2012 through November 18, 2012 as
Entrepreneurship week in the City of Lomita.

3. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve agenda.  Councilmember Traina seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that some street repairs were completed at the Lucille Street due to
the immediate safety issues regarding the street condition.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina thanked City Manager and staff for follow-up regarding broken street
lights and making sure that those were repaired. Councilmember Traina asked City Council to
consider changing the procedure of how Council-requested items are placed on a future City
Council agenda and set up a fair system without requiring three Councilmembers to agree for
placing agenda item on the agenda. According to Councilmember Traina, Councilmembers
should be able to bring forward matters for discussion that would not require staff to prepare
staff reports for the items, especially for the items that were requested by residents through the
Councilmembers. Councilmember Traina suggested rethinking the policy for placing items on
the agenda, and perhaps setting up certain parameters, such as possibly limiting the number of
items per Councilmember per meeting or month.

Mayor Gazeley replied that the current policy approved by the City Council states that once the
Council voted on the item it could not be brought back for a year. Mayor Gazeley added that
this matter of placing items on the future City Council agenda was discussed less than 10
months ago and the Council decision at that time was not to change the policy. Mayor Gazeley
disagreed with Councilmember Traina and stated that majority vote of the City Council is the
democratic process. Mayor Gazeley asked City Manager how long it takes for staff to prepare a
staff report when item is placed on the agenda. City Manager Rock responded that it varies
depending on the topic for discussion and research required for the staff report to be put
together.
  Page 2 of 8
 Councilmember Traina clarified that it should not require staff preparation if Council requests
discussion only agenda item. Discussion followed whether City Council would like to change the
current agenda item request policy.

Councilmember Traina moved to place to future City Council agenda reconsideration of the
current policy of how items are placed on the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion.

Comments were made by the Councilmembers that this agenda item request is not consistent
with the the current policy that require a year term for reconsideration of the item while agenda
item policy was discussed within last 10 months.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmember Traina
NOES: Councilmembers Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan and Mayor Gazeley

Councilmember Sanchez announced that C.E.R.T. meeting was scheduled for November 15,
2012, at 6pm at City Hall.

Mayor Gazeley informed residents that South Bay Environmental Services Center will be trading
up to two working strings of old electricity incandescent holiday lights for two new, energy-
efficient LED strings on November 13, 14, 15, and 16 from 9am to 5pm at South Bay
Environmental Services Center, 20285 S. Western Avenue, Suite 100, Torrance, CA 90501.
Residents must be South California Edison customers and bring utility bill or driver’s license.

Mayor Gazeley stated that if street lights are not working, residents need to report broken lights
to South California Edison and the street lights will be repaired within 5 days.

Mayor Gazeley added that at last SCAG meeting some representatives were concerned with AB
109 regarding current public safety realignment.

Councilmember Savidan relayed that residents commended Public Works Department Director
Damasse and his crew regarding timely and efficient response to the street problem at Lucille
Avenue.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Michael Jenquin, Lomita resident, stated that parking in Lomita is becoming a problem and
urged City Council to approve oversized vehicle ordinance.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, agreed with Councilmember Traina that City Councilmembers
should be able to bring forward items for discussion when requested by residents.

Sean Ritchie, Lindsey McAngus and Kacey Mather, Lomita part-time employees, were troubled
that the overtime was taken away from part-time employees and asked City Council to consider
changing the city policy regarding overtime.

  Page 3 of 8
 City Manager Rock responded that part-time employees are not eligible for the overtime pay
and therefore, work schedules for part-time employees will be flexed to eliminate overtime pay.
City Manager Rock stated that past practice has been discontinued due to the incorrect
interpretation of the labor law and from now on staff will make sure that the correct procedures
are followed. Discussion followed of who approves overtime, and whether holiday pay is paid to
part-time employees.

Mayor Gazeley suggested to the employees to go through the supervisor and meet with the City
Manager regarding this issue. City Manager Rock added that staff met with Union
Representative and he was in agreement with the management decision of eliminating overtime
for part-time employees.

Janet Gunter, San Pedro Peninsular Homeowners United representative, warned City Council
regarding possible health and safety hazards posed by the “Rancho” Liquid Petroleum Gas
Facility” located in San Pedro and urged City Council to get involved in this matter. City
Manager Rock stated that he is working with other City Managers on this issue and would report
back to the City Council shortly.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the Consent Agenda and asked to pull item 7.K for
discussion. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Estrada recommended purchasing newer vehicle instead of the recommended
2004 vehicle. Public Works Director Damasse responded that South Bay MDM mechanic
inspected both vehicles and his recommendation was to go with 2000 vehicle based on the
overall condition of the vehicle.

Councilmember Traina commended Director Damasse Vince for being economical. Discussion
followed whether the vehicle would last for a while and would be safe for the employees.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve purchase of the 2000 Ford Ranger truck in the
amount of $4,995 and the sale /auction of a 2002 Econoline van for the Public Works
Department. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Gazeley
Noyes: Councilmembers Estrada and Savidan.

Captain Blain Bolin provided update on the crime statistics in Lomita and stated that residential
burglaries are down 8%, but grand theft auto and larceny thefts in vehicles went up.

Chief Flores, Local Battalion Chief Station #6, updated regarding wild fires and preparedness.
Mayor Gazeley commented Fire Department for quick response time with the recent incident he
encountered with one of his neighbors.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  Page 4 of 8
   b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on
  October 15, 2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Report dealing with economic development activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Report dealing with activities of the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE
  AND FILE.

  f. Report dealing with activities of the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Report dealing with activities of the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE
  AND FILE.

  h. Report presenting the Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i.  Approval of Public Safety and Traffic Commission recommendation for installation
  of red curb at the terminus of Avocado Street north of 259th Place. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  j.  Approval of Public Safety and Traffic Commission recommendation for the
  extension of commercial loading zone on the west side of Cypress Street South of
  Pacific Coast Highway for “South Bay Triumph” (Motorcycles) at 2300 Pacific
  Coast Highway. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  k. Approval of the purchase of a used 2000 Ford Ranger truck in the amount of
  $4,995 and the sale/auction of a 2002 Econoline van for the Public Works

  l.  Review and update regarding current City of Lomita Film Permit Ordinance.

  m. Report submitting final Acceptance of Phase 1B Waterline Replacement and Street
  and accepting the work performed by Sully-Miller Contracting Company.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

8. CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (FY 2012-2017)

Public Works Director Damasse provided power point presentation (Attachment 1). Director
Damasse stated that the purpose of Capital Improvement Program (CIP) is to identify capital
projects and funding sources, and to allow staff strategically plan and prioritize projects within a
budget to maximize the efficient use of funds as well as preserve existing publicly-owned
property and infrastructure. Director Damasse talked about deteriorating street conditions and
aging pipes that need to be replaced. As a result the main projects identified for the 2012-2013
include: water and street improvement project (Eshelman Avenue from PCH to Lomita
Boulevard), West Basin 7 & 8 Import Water Connection Upgrades and Citywide Water Master
Plan update. Director Damasse pointed out that the City has sufficient funding for 80% of

  Page 5 of 8
 Eshelman project with the shortfall being proposed to be covered by the use of the reserve fund.
As for 2013-2017, Director Damasse stated that funding is not identified.

Parks and Recreation Department Director Harding provided overview of the proposed parks
and recreation projects and added that the majority of the proposed projects are unfunded. For
2012-2013 staff would like to be able to fund citywide facilities master plan and installation of the
emergency generator.

Administrative Services Director Chavez stated that Administrative Services Department would
like to upgrade financial system software utilized by the City with the addition of Payroll and
Personnel Modules in an amount of $50,000.

Councilmember Traina commended staff and City Manager Rock for CIP presentation and
added that it would be nice to include 254th and 241st streets in the CIP as well.

Councilmember Traina asked staff to look into possibility of applying for grants and lobbing out
representatives for CIP funding. City Manager Rock responded that State is looking at
increasing vehicle registration fees, which would help with street repairs and another option
could be to go to voters of Lomita and ask for special assessment to cover street maintenance
costs.

Discussion followed whether update to Water Master Plan is necessary when federal funding is
very limited. City Manager Rock noted that Water Master Plan is needed for internal purposes
and it is a state requirement to keep Water Master Plan updated.

Councilmember Traina asked staff to follow up with South California Edison regarding possibility
of replacing wooden poles with more esthetic ones while construction is performed on
Eshelman. Councilmembers thanked staff for well prepared and easy to read and understand
Capital Improvement Program.

Mayor Gazeley opened public input at 9:21pm. There were none.

Councilmember Estrada moved to authorize staff to finalize the proposed 5-year CIP for
possible adoption at the November 19, 2012 City Council meeting. Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

9. INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE RELATING TO AMENDMENT OF SALE OF ALCOHOLIC
  BEVERAGES - ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2012-03

Assistant City Manager/Community Development Director Sugano provided overview of the
agenda report and noted that in order for any business within the City to sell alcohol beverages,
that business must receive Conditional Use Permit approved by the Planning Commission with
five findings that are required for CUP applications, in addition to the requirements set in
Municipal Code Article 56. One of the findings could not be completed as required by Planning
Commission since countywide average of the crime statistics is not kept by the county and
therefore, could not be obtained. Staff recommended either the removal of the requirement for
the up-to-date crime statistics of any type or use modified finding proposed by the staff.

  Page 6 of 8
 Discussion followed of why crime statistics is not available through the county. City Attorney
Hogin clarified that the proposed change eliminates a very technical/specific requirement of
crime statistic that county does not keep, however, that change in the municipal code as
recommended does not change of what could be considered by the Planning Commission.
After discussion City Council agreed to include modified finding proposed by staff.

Mayor Gazeley opened public hearing.

Kevin Franklin, representing applicant, stated that the proposed business operation is a small
operation and not going to be an issue for the surrounding area. Mayor Gazeley closed public
input.

Councilmember Savidan moved to introduce first reading of the ordinance as prepared by staff
with one change. In Section 2 of the Ordinance, the three findings in Section 11-1.56.03(D)
were amended to read as follows:

  1. That the proposed use will not have an adverse impact on public safety. Factors that
  could be considered to determine impact include but are not limited to Los Angeles
  County crime statistics for the underlying and surrounding reporting districts, Los
  Angeles County Sheriff or other police agency crime statistics for the underlying and
  surrounding properties and the types of crime within those same areas;

  2. The business will provide beneficial commercial vitality to the area; and

  3. The use will not be objectionable or detrimental to surrounding properties and the
  neighborhood.

Councilmember Estrada seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

After further discussion Councilmember Savidan moved to approve a motion stating the City
Council’s intent that the amended ordinance did not satisfy the condition of approval for CUP
No.279 that required the removal of the crime statistic finding as proposed in Zone Text
Amendment No. 2012-03. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

10. CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING WORKSHOP

City Manager Rock asked City Council to establish a date for the City Council Strategic Planning
Workshop. Councilmember Estrada moved to schedule City Council Strategic Planning
Workshop for February 13, 2013, from 4pm to 9pm. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

11. CITYWIDE DRAINAGE MASTER PLAN

Public Works Director Damasse stated that staff was previously directed by City Council to
investigate local flooding issues. In 2005 Los Angeles County completed citywide hydrology
study following City Council approval of funding for the study in the amount of $275,000. After

  Page 7 of 8
 the study the City completed improvements to the City owned storm drain located at the 2023
262nd street. The rest of the storm drains in Lomita are county owned, and improvements to
those storm drains were not approved by the county since do not provide a regional benefit.
Therefore, if the City wants to have the remainder or a portion of these improvements
completed, it would need to be funded by the City. Director Damasse concluded that since the
hydrology/drainage study was completed in 2006, in staff’s opinion, no new citywide drainage
study master plan is needed at this time.

Councilmember Estrada moved to go with the staff recommendation to receive and file this
report. Mayor Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 10:01 p.m.

Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
